holidays.name: National Scrabble Day
holidays.description: A day for word nerds to dust off the tiles, hunt for triple-word scores, and argue over whether 'qi' is really a word (it is). Families and friends gather around the board to play and to dispute the dictionary.
holidays.origin: Observed on the birthday of Alfred Mosher Butts, born April 13, 1899, the architect who invented the game in 1938 during the Great Depression after losing his job. He originally called it 'Lexiko' and later 'Criss-Crosswords' before it became Scrabble.
holidays.funFact: Butts determined the letter distribution by counting letters on the front page of The New York Times, which is why there are 12 E's but only one Z.

holidays.name: National Peach Cobbler Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the warm, bubbly, buttery dessert topped with golden biscuit or cake-like crust. Best enjoyed with a scoop of vanilla ice cream melting over the top.
holidays.origin: Peach cobbler is a classic American dessert with roots in early settlers who lacked the equipment to make traditional English puddings, so they improvised by topping stewed fruit with biscuit dough. The day is an unofficial food observance popularized by food calendars.
holidays.funFact: The name 'cobbler' may come from the cobbled, bumpy look of the biscuit topping, which resembles a cobblestone street.

holidays.name: International Plant Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A leafy holiday for thanking the green things that keep us alive, from towering oaks to that sad office succulent you keep forgetting to water.
holidays.origin: This observance is a modern, grassroots celebration encouraged by gardeners and plant lovers to promote awareness of plants' role in ecosystems, and gaining popularity through social media and the houseplant boom.
holidays.funFact: Plants can't scream, but studies have found that stressed tomato and tobacco plants emit ultrasonic clicks and pops that microphones can detect.

holidays.name: Make Lemonade Day Eve? No — Thomas Jefferson's Birthday
holidays.description: Americans celebrate the birthday of the third U.S. president, a man who wrote the Declaration of Independence, designed his own house, and was obsessed with wine, books, and gadgets. Quirky observers mark it with macaroni and cheese and ice cream.
holidays.origin: Jefferson was born April 13, 1743. Jefferson's birthday is a federal-recognized observance in some states, and his love of French cuisine helped popularize dishes like macaroni and cheese and ice cream in America.
holidays.funFact: Jefferson owned a polygraph machine, a device that made a duplicate copy of whatever he wrote with one pen as he wrote with another.

holidays.name: International Day of Pplanes? No — Rock Day
holidays.description: A day for geology enthusiasts to hug a boulder, admire a pebble, and appreciate the humble rock that makes up the planet beneath our feet.
holidays.origin: Rock Day is an informal observance celebrated by geology fans and teachers as an excuse to get kids excited about earth science and collecting stones.
holidays.funFact: Some rocks, like pumice, are so full of gas bubbles that they can float on water for years, drifting across oceans on giant rafts.
